candidates.exact_span: The low flow or 4Q3 was taken from the previous permit and was provided by NMED.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the cited 4Q3 is treated as the operative receiving-flow input for limit derivation, or as provisional pending updated NMED values, changes the critical-dilution calculation and thus which TRC limit is selected as applicable.

candidates.exact_span: The 4Q3 is 431.3 cubic feet per second (cfs) and the harmonic mean low flow used for human health calculations is 1108 cfs. To convert 4Q3 expressed in cfs to 4Q3 expressed as MGD, the constant 1.548 cfs/MGD is used. The 4Q3 is 278.6 MGD and the harmonic mean low flow is 715.8 MGD.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Qa (4Q3) and the cfs-to-MGD conversion constant are inputs to the critical-dilution formula; different numeric values or flow measures would change the dilution-based chronic TRC concentration and whether the 19 ug/l acute or 11 ug/l chronic standard governs.

candidates.exact_span: The NMWQS for total residual chlorine (TRC) are 11 ug/l for chronic and 19 ug/l for acute conditions. The NNWQS for TRC are 4000 ug/L for domestic water supply, and primary/secondary human contact; 19 ug/L for aquatic & wildlife habitat-acute; and, 11 ug/L for aquatic & wildlife habitat-chronic and livestock watering.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which water-quality standard categories and numeric values are deemed applicable (including whether the NNWQS label is operative or a typographical reference to NMWQS) determines the candidate limits compared in the most-stringent-limit selection.

candidates.exact_span: Since acute conditions do not allow dilution; the limit must be met at end-of-pipe but chronic standards do allow dilution, the permit shall use the most stringent WQS for the permit limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when dilution may be applied versus when end-of-pipe compliance is required governs whether chronic or acute standards are evaluated and which numeric limit is enforceable.

candidates.exact_span:
Qe = facility effluent or design flow; 6.67 MGD
Qa = 4Q3; 278.6 MGD
F = fraction of stream allowed for mixing; 1.0
candidates.computation_change_reason: Effluent flow, receiving-flow, and mixing-fraction inputs directly determine critical dilution (CD) and therefore the dilution-adjusted chronic TRC concentration used in limit selection.
The computed critical-dilution fraction is the intermediate value used to derive the in-stream chronic TRC concentration; a different CD would change which standard is found more stringent.

candidates.exact_span:
The in-stream TRC concentration after allowing for dilution is; 11 ug/l ÷ 0.0234 = 470 ug/l.
Since this value is greater than the 19 ug/l end-of-pipe acute standard, the 19 ug/l is more
stringent and will be more protective. The draft permit maintains the 19 ug/l end-of-pipe acute
limit since it is more stringent and will be more protective than the 11 ug/l dilution based chronic
limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage states the comparison logic and the selected enforceable numeric TRC limit; alternative readings of the arithmetic or stringency test would change the applicable discharge limit used for compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span:
In addition to the 19 ug/l chemical specific limitation, the draft permit also maintains the
narrative limit for total residual chlorine shall be “No Measurable.” TRC shall be limited as
follows: “After dechlorination and prior to final disposal, the effluent shall contain NO
MEASURABLE (TRC) at any time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the narrative no-measurable limit is an additional enforceable limit alongside the 19 ug/l numeric cap affects which limit applies to reported measurements and how non-detect or missing numeric results are classified.

candidates.exact_span:
NO MEASURABLE will be defined as no detectable
concentration of TRC as determined by any approved method established in 40 CFR Part 136.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The detection-threshold and approved-method scope define when a measurement exceeds the narrative limit and how below-detection or method-specific non-results are interpreted for compliance and missing-evidence analysis.

candidates.exact_span:
The effluent limitation for TRC is the instantaneous maximum and cannot be averaged for
reporting purposes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Instantaneous-maximum versus averaging rules change how individual grab-sample results are compared to limits and what aggregation, if any, is permitted when assessing reported measurements and monitoring reports.

candidates.exact_span: The maximum dechlorinated TRC shall be monitored daily by grab sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Daily grab-sample frequency establishes the monitoring obligation schedule; interpretation of 'maximum dechlorinated TRC' and daily coverage affects whether missing days constitute unmet requirements or documented no-data states.

candidates.exact_span: TRC shall be measured within fifteen (15) minutes of sampling.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The hold-time requirement conditions whether a sample/analysis pair satisfies the monitoring protocol; late analyses could leave applicability of reported results unresolved for obligation and missing-evidence evaluation.

candidates.exact_span:
After dechlorination and prior to final disposal, the effluent shall contain NO
MEASURABLE (TRC) at any time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The temporal and process-location scope ('after dechlorination', 'prior to final disposal', 'at any time') determines which effluent events and sampling points fall under the limit and associated daily monitoring, affecting limit applicability, obligation windows, and classification of periods without qualifying measurements.
